items.answer: Extended Reality (XR) systems are highly interactive like other interactive systems, and consideration of human factors is important to understand how easily a user can provide input and perceive output.
Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

The major current application domains for virtual reality (VR) discussed are gaming and entertainment, healthcare, education, the automobile industry, travel and tourism (including virtual tourism and digital heritage preservation), real estate and architecture, and defense.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

A virtual reality (VR) system is defined by three characteristics: an artificial or synthetic environment, sensory experience through computer-generated stimuli, and user actions that partially determine what happens in the environment; a system with these aspects can be categorized as a virtual reality system and distinguished from other systems, which are not supposed to have these aspects.
